Four days where research meets practice.
about.p1: Why Culture Matters returns to Timișoara for its third edition, taking place from 7 to 10 October 2026 at FABER. Over four days, we bring together people who research, protect, interpret and pass on cultural heritage to discuss its role in contemporary society and why culture matters.
about.p2: Cultural heritage is more than the buildings, objects, places or traditions we have inherited. It shapes how we construct identity, memory and a sense of belonging, how we understand the past and relate to the present. And what we choose to protect, interpret or pass on says something about the kind of society we want to build.
about.p3: The 2026 edition approaches these questions through three interconnected themes: Heritage under Threat, Heritage Narratives and Heritage Literacy & Education. What happens when heritage comes under threat? How do we learn to recognise it, understand it and care for it? Who shapes the stories we tell about heritage, and how do these narratives influence what a community chooses to preserve, forget or pass on?
about.close: Cultural heritage is not only about our shared past; it is about how we choose to live together, now and in the future.
format.note: Why Culture Matters brings to the same table people who work with heritage from different perspectives, disciplines and contexts. It is a space for exchanging experience and ideas, and equally for examining concrete practice, testing methods and building new collaborations.

theme.1.title: Heritage under Threat
theme.1.question: How do we protect heritage in times of crisis and change?
theme.1.body: War, political instability, natural disasters, climate change, abandonment, real estate pressure and demographic shifts place cultural heritage under threat in different ways. Sometimes loss is sudden and visible; at other times, it happens slowly, through deterioration, neglect, or the disappearance of the functions and communities that give heritage meaning.
theme.2.title: Cultural Heritage Narratives
theme.2.question: Who tells the stories of heritage, and whose stories remain in our collective memory?
theme.2.body: The way we understand a place, a building, an object or a tradition is shaped by the stories we tell about them, but also by the voices we choose to listen to or overlook.
theme.3.title: Heritage Literacy & Education
theme.3.question: How do we learn to recognise, understand and care for heritage?
theme.3.body: Our relationship with heritage is shaped through education, experience and direct engagement with the places and stories around us. This section explores the role of schools, museums, cultural organisations and communities in developing this relationship, from formal and non-formal education to cultural mediation and participatory practices.
school.title: Cultural Heritage School
school.question: Eight pilot workshops for children, young people and adults.
school.body: Why Culture Matters 2026 marks the launch of the Cultural Heritage School, a new non-formal education initiative built around a simple idea: caring for heritage is something we learn.
school.more1: Not only by learning about history, architecture or art, but through direct engagement with heritage, through observation, questions, exploration and participation. The Cultural Heritage School aims to develop methods that enable children, young people and adults to discover, understand and build a relationship with the heritage around them.
school.more2: During Why Culture Matters 2026, the programme will be tested through eight pilot workshops, developed and led by invited professionals and educators. At the same time, the experiences and methodologies discussed in III. Heritage Literacy & Education will help shape the programme and its future direction.
school.more3: Why Culture Matters will thus become the first stage in testing and developing the Cultural Heritage School, before the programme is expanded in 2027.

about.p4: Through case studies, discussions and workshops, Why Culture Matters brings local and international experiences into dialogue, along with responses, methods and tools that can be put into practice.
about.p5: This edition also marks the beginning of the Cultural Heritage School, a non-formal education and cultural mediation programme that Asociația Prin Banat will develop from 2027 onwards, building in part on the ideas and formats tested during the symposium.
theme.1.body2: This section brings together experiences and case studies on protection, prevention, documentation, emergency preparedness, response and recovery, placing crisis situations in dialogue with less visible, but equally destructive, processes that affect cultural heritage over time.
theme.2.body2: This section explores how cultural heritage narratives are constructed, transmitted and reinterpreted, with particular attention to difficult, contested or forgotten histories, cultural mediation, and the role of communities in building new relationships with their own heritage.
theme.3.body2: We are interested in how heritage can become accessible, relevant and connected to everyday experience, and how, from one generation to the next, we can build the capacity to recognise, understand and protect it.
theme.3.more: The 2026 edition also introduces the Cultural Heritage School, a new educational initiative that will be piloted during the symposium and further developed from 2027 onwards.
